Commercial logging continues to destroy habitat and threatens the region's high biological diversity.

# Conservation of Nose-Touch Avoidance Across *C. elegans* and Relatives

Nose touch avoidance behavior is conserved among five of the six species tested (Figure 5A). In *C. tripartitum*, animals showed an overall avoidance rate of less than 10% after the first few positive trials, suggesting this species adapts to the nose-touch stimulus faster than *C. elegans* and the others (Figure 5A). During the first three trials, however, *C. tripartitum* responded quantitatively similarly to *C. elegans* (Figure S2 in Additional file 2).

Ablation of ASH neurons in five nose-touch responsive species eliminated nose-touch avoidance (Figure 5A). Four of the five species still showed some nose-touch responses in 20–30% of trials (Figure 5A). *Caenorhabditis* sp. 3 was the exception: its ASH-ablated animals completely lacked the ability to respond to nose touch (Figure 5A).

Ablation of the AWC neuron did not affect the response to nose touch in any of the species (Figure S3 in Additional file 2).

As shown in Fig. 15, the alitrunk is conspicuously swollen and sits much higher than the propodeal dorsum. The propodeum bears a pair of strong spines, straight to slightly upcurved. The metanotal groove is absent, and the metapleural lobes are triangular and conspicuous. In profile, the petiole has an elongate peduncle and a well-developed node whose dorsum slopes downward posteriorly, leaving a short posterior face. The anterior and dorsal surfaces of the postpetiole form a single convexity, with the posterior face truncated. In dorsal view, the nodes of both petiole and postpetiole are broader than long.

The dorsum of the head is strongly longitudinally rugose, with 5–7 rugae between the frontal carinae at eye level. The rugae are irregular and meander slightly, with a few anastomoses usually present. The scrobal area is largely smooth but usually has 1–2 fine rugulae crossing its width just behind the antennal fossa. The sides of the head behind the eyes are finely reticulate-rugose, and this sculpture continues around the posterior margins of the scrobe to the occiput. The spaces between rugae are unsculptured, or at most show faint superficial traces.

The dorsal alitrunk is finely but strongly reticulate-rugose throughout, with broad shining interspaces. The petiole dorsum is rugulose, while the postpetiole ranges from rugulose to only faintly sculptured. The gaster is unsculptured. All dorsal surfaces of the head and body are densely clothed with fine, acute hairs. Color ranges from dark reddish brown to blackish brown.

UPO-06: prhI Gene Synthesis
UPO-06 carries the coding sequence for *Ralstonia solanacearum* prhI, an ECF sigma factor needed for transcription driven by the Prh signal transduction system. PrhR activates the gene, which then directs sigma factor expression through activation of the PprhJ promoter. The sequence has been optimized for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

UPO-11: PprhJ Promoter Synthesis
UPO-11 contains the PprhJ promoter region. The promoter responds to plant cell contact through signal transduction mediated by PrhA and PrhR, and the ECF sigma factor PrhI activates it. The sequence has been optimized for expression in *Escherichia coli*.

Subject: foxl2 expression patterns in trout

Dear Customer,

Here is a summary of our findings on foxl2 transcript expression in your study.

Both foxl2 transcripts were expressed very early in development (Figure 2). foxl2a expression was highly restricted in the male, while the diverged paralog foxl2b was present in most adult extragonadal tissues examined (see Additional file 2).

foxl2b expression in adult female tissues was highly restricted, essentially confined to the skin, gill, and ovary. In the testis, foxl2b expression was very strong, which matches previous findings that foxl2b is present and foxl2a is absent in later stages of testis development in trout [23].

Taken together, these results suggest that foxl2b may regulate male-specific genes (such as cyp19b1), particularly later in development.

Renewable Energy Certificates (RECs) cannot support carbon neutrality claims for electricity use beyond a claimant's metered consumption. Most RECs come from projects that would have been financially viable without selling the certificates, so they lack additionality. Additionality is a counterfactual test: would the project have gone ahead anyway if the REC had not been purchased or contracted? Several testing frameworks exist, but they all ask the same basic question: did the project's finances depend on REC revenue? Without verified additionality, RECs are not equivalent to real emissions offsets.

We derived a time-dependent mild-slope equation from the formal derivation of Smith & Sprinks (1975), and from it obtained the higher-order dispersion relation for waves over an uneven bottom.

Using only the linear dispersion relation for steady waves, we recovered equation (2.12) of Chamberlain & Porter (1995), known as the Modified Mild-Slope Equation (MMSE). At leading order, the modified curvature terms of the MMSE have significant effects, while the slope square terms stay negligible, consistent with the mild-slope assumption. We therefore kept all the modified curvature terms that the MSE neglects, which gives a uniform model.

We built a numerical model with the finite element method (FEM) to predict wave scattering over a varying bottom. The uniform model captures the main features of waves over different sea beds, including sinusoidal beds and man-made bars. For sinusoidal beds, its results agree more closely with experimental data than other established models. For man-made bars, both the MMSE and the uniform model agree better with the data than Kirby (1986).

A further result of the FEM model is its application to wave transformation over arbitrarily varying bathymetry.

The description of the myth in the Phaedrus is the most intense of them all, though it belongs to a different order. It looks back to a former existence instead of forward to a future one, and it stages a conflict between reason, backed by passion or righteous indignation, and the animal instincts we are born with. Before birth, the soul traveled in the company of some god and saw truth in the form of the universal; our present life is the outcome of a struggle that came before. This earlier world is a relative construct, and it is often projected into the future instead, much as we wonder where men were before birth or what awaits them after death. The question "Where were men before birth?" feels unfamiliar and unnatural to us, yet it carries as much force and reaches as wide as the other. In the Phaedrus, the "spiritual combat" of this life is only a figure of speech, and the majesty and power of the whole passage, especially the proem beginning "The mind through all her being is immortal," cannot really be rendered in another language.

Subject: A Note on Buraq

Dear Friend,

For most of history, people saw no firm line between reality and myth; modern comparative biology drew that line. But science never erased the middle ground where a figure like Buraq lives, and we still need such transitional figures to connect empirical knowledge with spiritual experience.

Buraq sits between rationalist taxonomy and the older power of myth, and nowhere is this clearer than in the Islamic transport industry, where she recurs as a kind of patron saint combining piety and speed. She gives her name to airlines from Libya to Indonesia, bus companies, freight ships, motorcycle taxis, a space camp, an engineering college, and even Pakistan's first drone.

Part of why she works so well commercially is her fluidity as an aesthetic and linguistic object. She presides over wings and wheels, but also sells plastic and PVC, heavy metal, heavy-duty diesel (BURAQ LUBRICANTS), Indian food, and surgical instruments.

There are thousands of monsters roaming the world of MapleStory. Here's where they live and how to survive them.

**Weak monsters** are the most common foes, found near towns. They wander aimlessly even if you bump into them, so don't worry. Just take the damage.

The most dangerous monsters live deep in dungeons.

Monsters typically roam aimlessly even if you bump into them, but if you attack or cast a debuff on an enemy, you "aggro" it. That means you get its attention, and it will try to attack you back.

Most enemies attack by trying to run into you over and over again. Against these persistent attackers, the easiest thing to do is attack them repeatedly. Your attacks usually have enough knockback to keep them in place. Sometimes you'll need to jump over them to dodge their attacks entirely.

Aggro is a two-way street. Stay safe and keep attacking!

Someone who heard well enough to learn to speak and read will keep the ability to read even if their hearing later becomes too impaired to hear voices. A person who never heard well enough to learn to speak is rarely able to read proficiently (see [4]). Most evidence suggests that early identification of hearing impairment is key to helping a child with very insensitive hearing learn spoken language effectively. Transduction is how the nervous system turns physical and chemical signals into neural impulses. In sensory transduction, specialized receptors convert stimuli into electrical signals that travel to the brain.

The visual system shows this well. In the retina, rod and cone cells link the physical environment to neural communication. When light strikes these photoreceptors, it changes the shape of the protein rhodopsin. That change sets off a chain of events that alters the photoreceptor's electrochemical gradient. The reduced gradient means fewer electrical signals go to the brain. So more light hitting the photoreceptor results in fewer electrical impulses, and the brain works with that inverted signal to decode the visual world.

# Mobile gaming and co-creation

Mobile internet expands what storytelling can do in games through portable, location-aware interfaces. This is the latest step in a decades-long evolution of electronic games that try to make the player more than an avatar: a co-author alongside the original designers.

Location-aware interfaces let players fold real places into the gameworld and the gameworld back into real places, something no earlier interactive media could do. Beyond giving players a role in worldmaking, mobile games drop linear narratives for cooperative storytelling built on the player's experience of place.

The idea of the "author-player" is not new, but mobile games push it past the constraints of traditional video games. Because the worldmaking extends off the screen, these interfaces turn the player's sensory experience of real places into storytelling tools.

In our essay, we theorize the storytelling potential of mobile games and describe our attempt to use it in the design and implementation of our hybrid-reality game, University of Death.

Subject: Hitchhiking in the Ruhr Area, Germany

Dear Customer,

The Ruhr Area (German: Ruhrgebiet), often just called the Ruhr, is an urban region in North Rhine-Westphalia, Germany. It is made up of many former industrial cities, including Duisburg, Oberhausen, Bottrop, Mülheim an der Ruhr, Essen, Gelsenkirchen, Bochum, Herne, Hamm, Hagen, Dortmund, Recklinghausen, Unna, and Witten.

Around five million people live here, so the region is considerably larger than Berlin, Hamburg, or Munich. The motorway density is high, but hitchhiking can still be difficult because of the tangled network of minor roads. The main motorways are the A1, A2, and A3.

If you plan to hitch here, stay on those primary motorways. The smaller roads are hard to work with because hardly any transit traffic uses them. Germany is generally a pleasant country for hitchhiking, but the Ruhr Area is the most unpleasant part of it for that. Hitching inside the Ruhr is comparable to hitching in a big city like Istanbul: the cities are independent, but to a traveler they all feel like districts of one huge city.

We hope this helps you plan your trip.

Below are the key findings from our analysis of lung tissue volume and functional changes.

Total lung tissue volume was calculated as: volume of lung tissue = number of voxels × volume of the voxel, provided the compartment considered has a CT number above zero.

The change in functional residual capacity resulting from PEEP withdrawal (ΔFRC) was computed as the difference in total gas volume in the whole lung between PEEP and ZEEP states. Alveolar derecruitment was defined as the difference in gas volume within poorly aerated and nonaerated lung regions between these same conditions.

We also computed the changes in gas volume from PEEP withdrawal specifically in normally aerated lung regions, which were characterized by CT attenuations between -500 and -900 HU (see Figure 2).
